en.greeting: Hi! Today we meet will: one small word for guessing the future, offering help, making promises and deciding things on the spot. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: will + verb
steps.text: You know going to for plans. Now meet its partner, **will**.
steps.body: After **will**, use the **base form** of the verb (the verb as in the dictionary): **no to**, **no -ing**, **no -s**. *I will call*, *she will call*: the same for every **subject** (who does it: *I, Rina, my parents*). **am/is/are** become **be**: *It will be hot*, not 'It will is hot'. When speaking, **will → 'll** (*I'll, she'll*). **will not → won't**: an exception (not 'willn't'). Say it like *don't* with a w ('wount'), not like *want* (mau).

steps.title: Guessing the future
steps.text: A **prediction** is what you think will happen. Start with **I think**, **Maybe** or **I'm sure**.
steps.body: **Maybe** goes at the start. *I don't think Budi will come* sounds more natural than *I think Budi won't come*: English puts the *not* on *think*, even though Indonesian says *Saya rasa Budi tidak akan datang*.

examples.en: I think it will rain this afternoon.
examples.id: Saya rasa nanti sore akan hujan.

examples.en: Maybe the bus will be late.

examples.id: Saya yakin kamu akan suka Bandung.

examples.en: Jakarta will be very hot tomorrow.
I don't think Budi will come to the party.
examples.id: Saya rasa Budi tidak akan datang ke pesta.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Make a prediction about Rina.

question.prompt: Rina is sick today. Complete: I think she ___ at home tomorrow.
question.explanation: After **will**, always use the base form: **will stay**. No -s, even with *she* ('will stays'), and no -ing ('will staying').

steps.title: Offers and promises
steps.text: **will** also helps people. Offer help, or give your word.
steps.body: **Offer** (menawarkan bantuan): you see a problem and say **I'll** + verb: *You're busy? I'll help you.* **Promise** (janji): **I'll** … or **I won't** …, and **I promise** makes it stronger. Indonesian trap: we say *Nanti saya telepon* or *Biar saya yang bayar* with no *akan*, so learners say 'I call you later'. In English, offers and promises need will: **I'll call you later. I'll pay.**

steps.title: Build the promise
steps.text: You arrive at the office at 9:30. Your boss is not happy.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saya tidak akan terlambat lagi.
question.explanation: A promise with **won't** (will not) + the base form **be**: you need *be* before *late*, like *I am late* now. **again** goes at the end.

steps.title: Deciding right now
steps.text: Use **will** when you decide **at the moment you speak**: something happens, and you choose what to do.
steps.body: The phone is ringing → *I'll answer it.* Your friend says *There's no sugar* → *Oh, I'll buy some.* At a warung, you look at the menu → *I'll have the soto ayam, please.* Indonesian trap: we say *Saya angkat* or *Saya beli* with no future word, but English needs **'ll** here: 'The phone's ringing. I answer it' is wrong.

pairs.en: I'll have the soto ayam, please.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You're buying a shirt at a shop in Bandung.

question.prompt: Shop assistant: 'The blue shirt is Rp150.000 and the white one is Rp120.000.' You: 'Hmm… ___ the white one, please.'
question.explanation: You look at the prices and decide **now**, so use **will**: **I'll take the white one.** 'I take' is *saya ambil* word by word, with no future, and there's never *to* after will.

steps.title: Now or before?
steps.text: Indonesian **akan** covers both will and going to. So don't look at the Indonesian word: look at **when you decide**.

timeline.title: When do you decide?
timeline.caption: Plan from before (you already have the tickets) → going to. Decision right now (the phone is ringing) → will. Both talk about later.

marks.label: before: you make a plan → going to

steps.title: Plan or new decision?
steps.text: Budi sees plane tickets in Rina's hand.

question.prompt: Budi: 'Wow! What are these for?' Rina: 'I ___ my aunt in Bali next month.'
question.explanation: Rina already has the tickets: the plan is **from before**, so use **going to**: *I'm going to visit my aunt.* (**will** is for deciding at this moment, and it never takes *to*.) 'I visit' doesn't show the future.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in will.

flashcards.back: the base form: will go, will be, will call (bentuk dasar)
won't (tidak akan), said like 'don't' with a w

flashcards.back: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.

flashcards.front: Promise: Saya janji tidak akan lupa.
flashcards.back: I promise I won't forget. (Saya janji tidak akan lupa.)

flashcards.front: Decision now: HP-nya bunyi. Saya angkat.
flashcards.back: The phone's ringing. I'll answer it.

flashcards.front: Plan from before: I have the tickets. We ___ (watch) the film on Saturday.
flashcards.back: We're going to watch the film on Saturday. (rencana dari sebelumnya)

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita berkenalan dengan will: satu kata kecil untuk menebak masa depan, menawarkan bantuan, berjanji, dan memutuskan sesuatu saat itu juga. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: will + kata kerja
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu going to untuk rencana. Sekarang kenalan dengan pasangannya, **will**.
steps.body: Setelah **will**, pakai **bentuk dasar** kata kerja (kata kerja seperti di kamus): **tanpa to**, **tanpa -ing**, **tanpa -s**. *I will call*, *she will call*: sama untuk semua **subjek** (siapa yang melakukan: *I, Rina, my parents*). **am/is/are** menjadi **be**: *It will be hot*, bukan 'It will is hot'. Saat bicara, **will → 'll** (*I'll, she'll*). **will not → won't**: ini pengecualian (bukan 'willn't'). Ucapkan seperti *don't* dengan w ('wount'), bukan seperti *want* (mau).

steps.title: Menebak masa depan
steps.text: **Prediksi** adalah apa yang menurutmu akan terjadi. Awali dengan **I think** (saya rasa), **Maybe** (mungkin) atau **I'm sure** (saya yakin).
steps.body: **Maybe** ditaruh di awal kalimat. *I don't think Budi will come* terdengar lebih alami daripada *I think Budi won't come*: bahasa Inggris menaruh *not* pada *think*, walaupun bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya rasa Budi tidak akan datang*.

examples.en: I think it will rain this afternoon.
examples.id: Saya rasa nanti sore akan hujan.

examples.en: Maybe the bus will be late.

examples.id: Saya yakin kamu akan suka Bandung.

examples.en: Jakarta will be very hot tomorrow.
I don't think Budi will come to the party.
examples.id: Saya rasa Budi tidak akan datang ke pesta.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Buat prediksi tentang Rina.

question.prompt: Rina sakit hari ini. Lengkapi: I think she ___ at home tomorrow.
question.explanation: Setelah **will**, selalu pakai bentuk dasar: **will stay**. Tanpa -s, walaupun subjeknya *she* ('will stays'), dan tanpa -ing ('will staying').

steps.title: Menawarkan bantuan dan berjanji
steps.text: **will** juga dipakai untuk membantu orang. Tawarkan bantuan, atau berikan janjimu.
steps.body: **Offer** (menawarkan bantuan): kamu melihat ada masalah dan bilang **I'll** + kata kerja: *You're busy? I'll help you.* **Promise** (janji): **I'll** … atau **I won't** …, dan **I promise** membuatnya lebih kuat. Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: kita bilang *Nanti saya telepon* atau *Biar saya yang bayar* tanpa *akan*, jadi pelajar bilang 'I call you later'. Dalam bahasa Inggris, tawaran dan janji butuh will: **I'll call you later. I'll pay.**

steps.title: Susun janjinya
steps.text: Kamu sampai di kantor jam 9.30. Atasanmu tidak senang.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Saya tidak akan terlambat lagi.
question.explanation: Janji dengan **won't** (will not) + bentuk dasar **be**: kamu butuh *be* sebelum *late*, seperti *I am late* untuk sekarang. **again** ditaruh di akhir.

steps.title: Memutuskan saat itu juga
steps.text: Pakai **will** saat kamu memutuskan **tepat saat berbicara**: sesuatu terjadi, lalu kamu memilih apa yang mau kamu lakukan.
steps.body: HP berdering → *I'll answer it.* Temanmu bilang *There's no sugar* → *Oh, I'll buy some.* Di warung, kamu melihat menu → *I'll have the soto ayam, please.* Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: kita bilang *Saya angkat* atau *Saya beli* tanpa kata masa depan, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **'ll** di sini: 'The phone's ringing. I answer it' itu salah.

pairs.en: I'll have the soto ayam, please.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu sedang membeli kemeja di sebuah toko di Bandung.

question.prompt: Pramuniaga: 'The blue shirt is Rp150.000 and the white one is Rp120.000.' Kamu: 'Hmm… ___ the white one, please.'
question.explanation: Kamu melihat harganya lalu memutuskan **sekarang**, jadi pakai **will**: **I'll take the white one.** 'I take' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *saya ambil*, tanpa masa depan, dan setelah will tidak pernah ada *to*.

steps.title: Sekarang atau sebelumnya?
steps.text: Kata **akan** dalam bahasa Indonesia mencakup will dan going to. Jadi jangan lihat kata Indonesianya: lihat **kapan kamu memutuskan**.

timeline.title: Kapan kamu memutuskan?
timeline.caption: Rencana dari sebelumnya (kamu sudah punya tiketnya) → going to. Keputusan saat ini juga (HP sedang berdering) → will. Keduanya membicarakan nanti.

marks.label: sebelumnya: kamu membuat rencana → going to

steps.title: Rencana atau keputusan baru?
steps.text: Budi melihat tiket pesawat di tangan Rina.

question.prompt: Budi: 'Wow! What are these for?' Rina: 'I ___ my aunt in Bali next month.'
question.explanation: Rina sudah punya tiketnya: rencananya **dari sebelumnya**, jadi pakai **going to**: *I'm going to visit my aunt.* (**will** untuk keputusan saat itu juga, dan tidak pernah diikuti *to*.) 'I visit' tidak menunjukkan masa depan.

steps.title: Ulasan singkat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini supaya will makin melekat.
